title: Runtime: bounded request queues + deterministic shed points (prefill/decode) with explicit reasons
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Context
Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding requires deterministic shed points in the runtime to prevent queue blowups, KV-cache thrash, and tail-latency collapse under overload. This ticket implements bounded queues + explicit shed reasons at runtime scheduling boundaries (prefill/decode) to complement gateway/routing admission control.

Problem
Today the runtime accepts work faster than it can schedule when GPU pools are saturated. This results in:
- unbounded in-memory queue growth (and increased GC / allocator pressure)
- request timeouts that look like internal failures
- streaming connections that disconnect mid-flight due to backlog
- latency spirals when prefill and decode scheduling compete for limited resources

Goals
- Bound request backlog inside the runtime per (model, gpu_pool, priority_class) to cap memory + prevent latency spirals.
- Add deterministic shed points at:
  1) enqueue/admission into runtime worker
  2) prefill scheduling boundary
  3) decode scheduling boundary
- Return explicit, stable shed reasons so upper layers can map to consistent customer-facing errors (429/503 + Redwood error codes) and so SRE can alert on “protected overload” vs “internal failure”.
- Ensure behavior is safe for streaming: avoid partial responses with ambiguous failure modes; do not shed after we’ve begun sending tokens unless the connection is already broken.

Non-goals
- Rewriting the scheduler architecture or introducing a new global fairness model.
- Implementing customer-specific bespoke overload logic. This should be policy-driven by routing/gateway and surfaced as hints/priority classes.

Implementation plan (runtime)
1) Bounded queues
- Introduce a bounded queue per runtime instance keyed by (model_id, pool_id, priority_class).
- Default bounds tuned per model class (small/medium/large context) and hardware type.
- Overflow behavior: shed immediately with reason RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL (no waiting / no retry storm at runtime layer).

2) Deterministic shed points
- Shed on enqueue (fast path):
  - If queue at/over limit: shed reason RUNTIME_QUEUE_FULL.
  - If request already expired (deadline passed): shed reason DEADLINE_EXCEEDED_AT_ARRIVAL.
- Shed at prefill scheduling boundary:
  - If prefill queue at/over limit or predicted prefill time exceeds remaining deadline: shed reason PREFILL_QUEUE_FULL or PREFILL_DEADLINE_RISK.
  - If KV-cache/memory pressure signal indicates imminent thrash: shed reason MEMORY_PRESSURE (wired but thresholding may land in ENG-4827).
- Shed at decode scheduling boundary:
  - If decode backlog over limit: shed reason DECODE_QUEUE_FULL.
  - If streaming request is mid-stream: do not proactively shed; instead rely on connection close semantics. Only mark reason STREAM_ABORTED if client disconnects.

3) Reason codes + plumbing
- Emit a single “final decision” for each request: accepted | shed (with reason) | failed (with internal error).
- Add an internal enum for runtime shed reasons that maps 1:1 to the end-to-end overload reason codes being standardized across gateway→routing→runtime.

4) Observability
- Metrics (names tentative; final naming in ENG-4829):
  - runtime_queue_depth{model,region,pool,priority_class}
  - runtime_queue_capacity{model,region,pool,priority_class}
  - runtime_shed_total{reason,model,region,pool,priority_class}
  - runtime_shed_latency_ms{reason,...} (time from arrival to shed decision)
  - runtime_prefill_wait_ms / runtime_decode_wait_ms (distribution)
- Tracing:
  - add span event “runtime.shed” with attributes reason, stage (enqueue|prefill|decode), queue_depth, deadline_remaining_ms.

Acceptance criteria
- Under synthetic overload (step-function traffic) runtime memory stays bounded and queue depth plateaus at configured limits.
- p99 latency does not exhibit runaway growth when demand exceeds capacity; instead the shed rate increases and latency remains within a bounded band for accepted traffic.
- Shed reasons are deterministic, stable, and observable (metrics + traces).
- Integration tests cover:
  - shed at enqueue
  - shed at prefill boundary
  - shed at decode boundary
  - no proactive mid-stream shedding once tokens are being emitted

Open questions
- Priority classes: confirm mapping from routing hints to runtime priority_class (e.g., interactive vs batch; tier-based) with Mina/Ravi.
- Default queue capacities per model class: initial values from canary + perf tests; SRE to sign off for Hosted defaults.

Rollout
- Feature flag: enable bounded queues + shed points per (region, model) behind overload protection flag.
- Canary: us-east, 1–2 high-traffic models, compare: shed rate mix, p95/p99, OOM incidence, streaming disconnect rate.

Links
- Initiative: ENG-4821
- Related: ENG-4827 (memory-pressure/KV-cache guardrails), ENG-4829 (metrics/traces)
- PR (implementation): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18475
- PR (end-to-end reasons): https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18494
comments: 2025-11-04 (Lena Fischer): Drafted queue bounding design with two thresholds: hard cap for admission + soft cap to bias scheduler away from large prefills when backlog high. Soft cap might be overkill for v1; keeping scope to hard cap + deterministic shed points.

2025-11-07 (Omar El-Sayed): Please ensure shed-at-decode does not kill an already-streaming request. If we shed after a few tokens, customers see partial output + ambiguous retries. Prefer: only shed decode for non-streaming, or only before first token for streaming.

2025-11-12 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler boundary is the right place. Suggest stage tagging: enqueue|prefill_sched|decode_sched so we can debug where time is spent. Also add metric for time-in-queue separately from GPU execution time.

2025-11-18 (Tomáš Novák): From incident learnings: the biggest win is preventing queue growth that starves control-plane heartbeats and causes cascading retries. Please prioritize shed-early on arrival when queue is at limit (no waiting).

2025-11-25 (Lena Fischer): Implemented bounded queue with per-(model,pool,priority_class) capacity. Added shed-at-enqueue + shed-at-prefill boundary. Decode shed only applies pre-first-token for streaming requests; otherwise we rely on client disconnect. Added unit tests for each stage.

2025-12-02 (Allison Grant): Observability review: avoid high-cardinality labels (no request_id, no full route). Model should be a small bounded identifier, pool should be a bounded set. Please keep reason values enumerated and stable.

2025-12-06 (Marcus Reed): Perf characterization: with bounds enabled under overload, allocator pressure dropped and p99 for accepted traffic stabilized. However, initial cap was too low for long-context prompts and caused earlier-than-expected shedding. Adjusted defaults upward for large-context models; leaving final tuning to canary + SRE.

2025-12-10 (Ravi Menon): Routing will pass priority_class hint (interactive|batch) and deadline_ms. Runtime should treat missing hints as interactive by default. This matches gateway behavior and reduces surprise for SDKs.

2025-12-16 (Noah Patel): PR 18475 is up for review. Remaining items before merge: (1) align reason enum naming with gateway/routing spec in PR 18494, (2) confirm streaming pre-first-token shed behavior with SRE/PM, (3) ensure metrics names match ENG-4829 standard.
